Anthropic highlighted its commitment to responsible AI development, noting Singapore's high usage of its Claude model relative to population. The company also revealed 12 job openings as it expands its local team to support public and private sector clients.
items.title: Anthropic Opens Singapore Office and Signs AI Safety Agreement

items.summary: Demis Hassabis, co-founder of Google DeepMind, described recent AI-driven hacking incidents as early warning shots, cautioning that major security breaches could occur without improved safeguards. He noted that while current systems are not yet fully powerful, the risk escalates if the industry fails to adopt rigorous security practices and international standards. Microsoft's Brad Smith echoed the urgency, calling for balanced regulation to match rapid technological innovation.
items.title: Google DeepMind's Hassabis Warns of AI Hacking Risks

items.summary: Nvidia is donating $250m worth of computing power to the UK to support AI safety research over five years. The donation aims to bolster agentic safety and security research, with funds directed toward institutions including the British Open-Ended Learning and Discovery Lab and Imperial College London. Nvidia's CEO, Jensen Huang, highlighted the UK's scientific rigour in addressing this engineering challenge.
items.title: Nvidia donates computing power to UK for AI safety research

items.summary: Nvidia is investing nearly $10 billion in Europe, with a significant portion directed toward France, to bolster the nation's technological sovereignty. These investments target sectors including healthcare, robotics, and enterprise software. The strategy aligns with President Emmanuel Macron's push for European independence in the AI race against the United States and China. While Nvidia provides chips, partners like Foxconn and Bull are building the necessary infrastructure in Western France. Additionally, Nvidia is deploying open-weight AI models in French government and banking systems to ensure data remains under local control, aiming to create a sovereign digital ecosystem.
items.title: Nvidia Invests Billions in France to Support AI Sovereignty Amid US-China Race

items.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella discussed a 2008 or 2009 meeting with Bill Gates regarding an enterprise acquisition he viewed as flawed. Nadella admitted the experience haunts him because he failed to challenge the decision despite believing it was architecturally unsound. He now uses the memory to reflect on the difficulty of speaking up in important meetings when one sees a problem others miss.
items.title: Satya Nadella Reflects on Regretful Acquisition Meeting with Bill Gates

items.summary: Christopher Adam argues that resource-rich economies face a global scramble for critical minerals driven by energy transition, digital transformation, and defence needs. While demand is projected to quadruple by 2040, Adam warns against a 'resource curse' or 'presource curse' if countries fail to manage the windfall. He suggests that well-designed contracts, royalties, and industrial policy are essential to capture value beyond extraction, noting that China currently dominates global processing. Adam highlights the need for geological mapping, transparent contracts, and local content requirements to ensure lasting development rather than repeating historical mistakes.
items.title: Resource-rich economies must design contracts to turn critical mineral windfalls into lasting development

items.summary: Research indicates that strengthening social insurance collection in China reduced formal firm entry and shifted workers toward informal employment. While the reform increased compliance and payments, it also lowered new business registrations, profitability, and productivity. The study suggests that pairing collection enforcement with lower contribution rates and portable benefits could mitigate these negative effects on formal job creation and economic activity.
items.title: China's Stricter Social Insurance Collection Pushed Workers to Informal Jobs

items.summary: The International Energy Agency warns that global diesel and gasoil markets will face significant strain through 2027, with inventory replenishment unlikely before late next year. Record prices in Europe and the U.S. have reached roughly $220 a barrel. While a proposed deal aims to release 300,000 metric tons of Russian diesel, the IEA states this is insufficient to offset the deficit built during 2026.
items.title: IEA Warns of Tight Diesel Markets Through 2027 Amid Record Prices

items.summary: Getty Images announced an agreement with major lenders to restructure debt and go private through a prepackaged bankruptcy. The Getty Family and Koch Equity Development affiliates will invest up to US$533 million in new equity. Getty expects the restructuring to be complete by end 2026, with operations continuing normally and no anticipated impact on stakeholders.
items.title: Getty Images Announces Private Restructuring via Prepackaged Bankruptcy

items.summary: The EU stated there is no indication that US intelligence sharing with Ukraine has stopped, despite Kyiv's complaints about unannounced Starlink restrictions. Ukraine is seeking clarification from the US, SpaceX, and NATO regarding these limitations affecting drone operations.
items.title: EU and US officials deny halting intelligence sharing with Ukraine amid Starlink concerns

items.summary: A Liberty Street Economics post argues that the AI boom has not substantially impacted the U.S. current account deficit, despite rising imports of AI-related equipment. The author explains that the deficit is driven by the gap between saving and investment. While AI imports reached a high of 23 percent in 2025, aggregate investment has remained steady, and business saving has held up, unlike during the dot-com era. The widening deficit is attributed primarily to government dissaving rather than private saving or investment changes. However, the author notes that future increases in AI capital spending could eventually widen the deficit if other investment sectors continue to weaken.
items.title: AI Boom Has Not Yet Widened U.S. Current Account Deficit

items.summary: Google DeepMind and Google Cloud announced they will provide up to 200 European scientific researchers with direct access to their frontier models. The companies, based in the U.S., will also offer $3 million in compute credits. This initiative includes tools like AlphaFold 3 and AlphaEarth Foundations, aiming to help researchers tackle complex challenges such as predicting extreme weather patterns and mapping molecular structures more efficiently.
items.title: Google DeepMind and Google Cloud Grant European Researchers Access to Frontier Models

items.summary: Google has launched Gemini 4 Argon, a new AI model designed to solve complex engineering and scientific problems. Available globally today via API and specific Google platforms, Argon excels in coding, finance, legal, and cybersecurity domains. The model ranks #1 on the Vals Index and has already helped Google teams refactor large codebases and optimize workflows. External partners like Wiz and Gamow Labs are using it to secure infrastructure and analyze genomes. Google is offering free access to 10,000 scientists for six months and expanding the Fairwind Program for cybersecurity defenders. The model features enhanced safety measures, including reduced jailbreak success rates and improved agent alignment.
items.title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Argon for Complex Enterprise Tasks

items.summary: An article by Ruipeng Liu and Sagarika Mishra examines the 'circular financing' model driving the AI boom, where companies like Nvidia, Microsoft, Amazon, and Google act as investors, suppliers, and customers simultaneously. A central bank analysis found 55.2% of AI investments came from other AI firms. Nvidia exemplifies this, investing billions in OpenAI and guaranteeing data centers while securing them as customers. This concentration of risk complicates valuations and market stability, with chipmakers contributing 70% of S&P 500 gains in 2026. The Reserve Bank of Australia warns that opaque, debt-financed cycles could trigger a bubble burst if demand fails to materialize.
items.title: AI boom driven by circular financing between chipmakers and customers

items.summary: A Meerut court sentenced Muskan Rastogi and Sahil Shukla to death on October 14, 2026, for the murder of Saurabh Rastogi. Allegedly committed on March 3, 2025, the crime involved sedation, dismemberment, and concealment of remains in a blue drum. The trial concluded after 13 months and 126 hearings, with 22 witnesses examined by the prosecution.
items.title: Meerut Court Sentences Wife and Partner to Death in Blue Drum Case

items.summary: Turmeric prices in Erode reached ₹23,000 a quintal, their highest level in recent years, driven by lower arrivals and drought conditions in major growing regions. M. Sathyamurthy of the Erode Turmeric Merchants and Godown Owners' Association noted that water scarcity has reduced planted areas by 20% to 30% in some regions, with further declines expected. Futures on NCDEX for April 2027 trade between ₹24,000 and ₹25,000 a quintal.
items.title: Turmeric Prices Surge in Erode Amid Drought Concerns

items.summary: Chrystia Freeland, former Canadian trade minister, told Semafor that the EU and UK made a historic blunder by yielding to Trump administration tariff pressure during his second term. She argued this appeasement harms the Western alliance. Meanwhile, US-Canada trade relations have deteriorated, with Ottawa imposing counter-tariffs. Freeland noted that repairing ties may require waiting until Trump leaves office.
items.title: Former Canadian Trade Minister Criticizes EU and UK Tariff Decisions

items.summary: Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janata Party, was heckled at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport upon his return from a brief hometown visit. The crowd shouted, "Why are you ruining the country?" Dipke arrived a day after his party co-convenors, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. Rajeev Singh of The Times of India reported the incident.
items.title: CJP Founder Abhijeet Dipke Heckled at Delhi Airport Over Country Ruin

items.summary: Air India diverted a Frankfurt-Delhi flight to Jaipur after Mumbai air traffic control received a transponder code 7500, indicating hijacking. Pilots denied squawking the code, stating operations were normal. Security agencies conducted extensive checks on the aircraft, crew, and passengers, finding no issues. The flight was cleared to continue to Delhi.
items.title: Air India Flight Diverted After Hijack Code Alert

items.summary: Beijing plans to construct 100 habitat gardens and villages for ancient trees by 2030, according to an action plan from the Beijing Greening Commission. The initiative aims to protect the city's tens of thousands of century-old trees, with the oldest estimated at 3,500 years. The plan includes creating 10 ecological landmarks, restoring over 3,000 trees, and launching a third citywide survey to assess tree conditions and locations.
items.title: Beijing Plans 100 Ancient Tree Habitats by 2030

items.summary: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman stated that the Reserve Bank of India will continue measures to prevent excessive rupee volatility. She attributed recent depreciation to global uncertainties while noting strong domestic fundamentals. The RBI recently introduced a special window for oil marketing companies and tightened forex derivative rules. These actions supported the rupee, which appreciated to Rs 94.96 in early trade on Tuesday.
items.title: RBI Continues Efforts To Prevent Excessive Volatility In Value Of Rupee: FM

items.summary: UBS maintains a Buy rating on CarTrade Tech, citing a potential 5x revenue increase for OLX to Rs 11.8 billion by FY31. The brokerage attributes this upside to deeper monetisation strategies rather than GMV growth, drawing parallels to eBay's historical performance. CarTrade Tech has improved OLX's profitability and user experience since acquiring the platform.
items.title: UBS forecasts 5x revenue growth for OLX under CarTrade Tech

items.summary: The US surpassed 80,000 public EV fast-charging ports as of 2026, according to a report by Paren. While the total number of ports grew by 4,106 in Q3 2026, the pace slowed compared to the previous quarter. Tesla remained the leading network, adding 1,287 ports, but also raised its average non-member Supercharger price by 15% to 56.9 cents per kWh. Meanwhile, non-Tesla networks held steady around 53.3 cents per kWh. New stations are becoming larger and more powerful, with 73% of new ports rated at least 250 kW.
items.title: Tesla Leads US Fast-Charger Growth While Raising Prices

items.summary: IDBI Bank shares jumped to Rs 93.60 apiece, marking the highest level in nearly two weeks as the company's market capitalisation crossed Rs 1 lakh crore. This surge occurs while the long-running privatisation process moves closer to a conclusion, with Fairfax emerging as the frontrunner to acquire a combined stake of nearly 61%. The bank reported an 18% year-on-year increase in total business to Rs 6.27 lakh crore for the July-September quarter. Analysts from JM Financial note that while loan growth is accelerating, coverage NIMs are expected to contract due to FCNR-B inflows.
items.title: IDBI Bank Shares Rally Amid Privatisation Hopes and Strong Q2 Business

items.summary: Shoko Noda and Kamal Kishore of the United Nations argue that reducing housing risk is essential to lowering humanitarian needs. They note that disasters like floods in Nepal and earthquakes in Venezuela displace millions and strain resources. While 2026 humanitarian plans received only 30% of the requested $33.66 billion, the authors propose three priorities: expanding access to safe land, enforcing building codes, and making safer construction affordable. They cite examples from Ecuador, Vietnam, and Jamaica to illustrate how land-use planning, resilient design, and financing instruments can prevent displacement and protect communities before emergencies occur.
items.title: Experts urge reducing housing risk to lower humanitarian needs

items.summary: The Upper Siang district administration banned assemblies of five or more people amid protests against the 11,000 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project. Four protesters were detained under the UAPA, while civil society groups demanded their release and the withdrawal of Central Armed Police Forces. Authorities allege foreign funding for the movement, serving a notice to a legal advisor for unregistered funds. Residents oppose the dam, which would submerge 27 villages.
items.title: Assembly Ban and Detentions Spark Tensions Over Siang Dam Project

items.summary: Researchers in Telangana's Amrabad Tiger Reserve found shield-tailed snake remains in sloth bear scat, potentially marking the first record of bears hunting snakes. While sloth bears primarily eat insects, this discovery suggests dietary flexibility. The species is classified as vulnerable and protected under India's Wildlife Protection Act. Experts note that rocky hillocks serve as crucial refuges outside protected areas.
items.title: Sloth Bears Hunt Snakes in Telangana Forests

items.summary: The European Commission raised minimum prices for imported grain-oriented electrical steel (GOES) and transformer cores to protect the EU steel industry. While EU steelmakers support these measures, energy sector representatives argue that European producers cannot currently supply the necessary volume or quality of GOES. Consequently, they fear the restrictions will complicate supply chains and increase transformer production costs. The temporary measures are scheduled to expire in February 2027, pending a decision on their permanence.
items.title: EU Raises Steel Import Costs Amid Transformer Shortage

items.summary: The Calcutta High Court questioned authorities for allegedly denying CPI(M) permission to set up a bookstall in Bongaon while allowing others to erect temporary structures during Durga Puja. Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya directed an inquiry into the matter, stating that permissions cannot be granted or denied selectively. The court will hear the case again after receiving a police report and additional affidavits from the CPI(M).
items.title: Calcutta High Court Orders Inquiry Into Selective Denial of CPI(M) Bookstall Permission

items.summary: Kashim Chowdhury is on trial accused of fraud for allegedly holding five full-time public sector roles simultaneously between February 2020 and September 2023, earning approximately £350,000. Prosecutors claim he used sick notes and wore makeup during video calls to appear ill while working from home. Chowdhury denies acting dishonestly. The trial continues at Southwark Crown Court.
items.title: Civil Servant Accused of Fraud for Holding Five Jobs

items.summary: China's loneliness industry, valued at around $7.4 billion in 2025, facilitates paid companionship for elderly individuals facing isolation. Services range from meal delivery and household assistance to medical escorts, addressing gaps left by traditional support networks. Providers describe their roles as 'community children,' offering predictable relationships that alleviate emotional and practical burdens for seniors living alone.
items.title: China's Growing Market for Paid Companionship for the Elderly

items.summary: Rising prices of fine rice varieties are driving retail inflation in Tamil Nadu, which recorded the highest food inflation among major states at 10.62% in September. Prices for popular fine rice types surged from ₹50-60 to ₹70-90 per kg due to supply constraints caused by rainfall deficits in neighboring states like Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka. While overall rice supply remains adequate, specific fine varieties like Sanna are in short supply, forcing reliance on imports. Industry reports cite higher input costs and labor shortages as additional factors. The Tamil Nadu government is considering procuring fine rice to stabilize prices.
items.title: Rising Fine Rice Prices Fuel Inflation in Tamil Nadu

items.summary: Samaira Garg, a 16-year-old student, launched Made@gain to repurpose unused notebook sheets into new notebooks for students in need. Partnering with Rescript, the initiative converts collected paper into high-quality notebooks. Since its inception in February 2025, Made@gain has collected over 20,000 kilograms of stationery to create approximately 12,000 notebooks, distributing around 8,000 to students in schools and communities. The project has saved roughly 46,200 litres of water and prevented 1,368 kilograms of CO2 emissions. Garg continues to expand the program through school drives and corporate partnerships.
items.title: Student Samaira Garg Launches Notebook Recycling Initiative Made@gain

items.summary: Unico, a U.S. specialist in power conversion, launched its first inverter, the 330 kW bidirectional Grid-Tie Inverter. Developed in 2025, the platform supports solar generation and energy storage, operating at 98.5% efficiency. Unico CEO Mike Canada noted the growing demand for such technology in data centers and battery storage applications.
items.title: Unico Launches New 330 kW Bidirectional Grid-Tie Inverter

items.summary: The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, approved a 78-day Diwali bonus of Rs 2,009 crore for over 11.4 lakh non-gazetted railway personnel. The incentive recognizes Indian Railways' record performance in cargo and passenger transport. Concurrently, political tensions rose as CJP founder Abhijeet Deepke faced heckling at Delhi Airport following his return from Maharashtra, while other party leaders faced legal custody.
items.title: Union Cabinet Approves Diwali Bonus for Railway Staff Amid Political Tensions

items.summary: Assam's Juvenile Justice Board ordered a 17-year-old accused of raping and murdering a 16-year-old girl to be tried as an adult. Hailakandi police stated the principal magistrate made this decision based on the crime's heinous nature, psychological assessments, and medical reports. The victim was found dead on August 1. While the girl's family welcomed the decision, legal experts offered mixed reactions. Senior advocate Gautam Ghose supported the ruling, citing the brutality of the incident. Conversely, human rights lawyer Taniya Laskar argued that trying a minor as an adult violates human rights and urged adherence to statutory safeguards over public sentiment. The case has triggered widespread protests in the region.
items.title: Assam Court Orders Adult Trial for Juvenile Rape Accused

items.summary: K. Annamalai, founder of the We The Leaders movement, announced that the group will contest local body elections in Tamil Nadu. Speaking at a meeting in Mannargudi on October 13, 2026, he urged members to avoid "dirty politics" like switching sides before the indelible ink dries, citing the example of Mannargudi MLA S. Kamaraj. The statement was published on October 13, 2026.
items.title: We The Leaders to Contest Tamil Nadu Local Body Polls

items.summary: Advocate Krishan Kumar Dubey stated that Muskan Rastogi and Sahil Shukla appeared shocked after receiving the death penalty for killing ex-Merchant Navy officer Saurabh Rajput. Dubey described the crime as meticulously planned and noted the verdict's historic nature. The prosecution alleged Rajput's body was concealed in a blue drum. The couple faces fines totaling ₹70,000.
items.title: Advocate Reveals Shocked Reaction of Death Penalty Accused

items.summary: The US Supreme Court will hear arguments in Salazar v. Paramount Global regarding the Video Privacy Protection Act of 1988. The case determines whether the law protects users of non-video services, like email newsletters, when a video provider shares their viewing data. Michael Salazar, who sued Paramount over tracking tools used on 247Sports, argues the law covers all subscribers. Paramount contends protection applies only to direct video transactions. Lower courts have issued conflicting rulings, prompting the Supreme Court to intervene before its 2027 term concludes. The decision could significantly impact how media and technology companies collect and share user data.
items.title: Supreme Court to Decide Scope of 1988 Video Privacy Law

items.summary: The kidnapping of Sinaloa Cartel leader Ismael 'El Mayo' Zambada in July 2024 has generated conflicting narratives from former U.S. Ambassador Ken Salazar and Mexican President Andrés Manuel López Obrador. Salazar, in his memoir, claims the U.S. had no prior knowledge of the abduction and that Zambada was found sedated on a plane after Los Chapitos betrayed him. Conversely, López Obrador accuses the U.S. State Department and security agencies of orchestrating the operation with Los Chapitos, citing a letter from Salazar suggesting prior awareness. The incident triggered a violent two-year war between cartel factions, leaving hundreds dead and raising questions about U.S. involvement in Mexican sovereignty.
items.title: Competing Accounts of El Mayo Zambada's Kidnapping

items.summary: A painting purchased by New York teacher Helene Plotkin for under $100 in 1966 sold for £189,200 at a Lyon & Turnbull auction in June 2026. Originally misidentified as 'Portrait of Miss Don Wauchope' and bought at Christie's for £21 in 1966, the work was recognized as a 1920s piece by Francis Campbell Boileau Cadell. Plotkin's son, Barry, used Google's Gemini AI to decipher the signature, leading specialists to confirm the attribution and correct the subject's name to May Easter. The sale, reported by Artnet News as approximately $254,000, included the buyer's premium and exceeded the pre-sale estimate of £150,000 to £200,000.
items.title: Thrift Store Painting Sells for £189,200 After Six Decades

items.summary: A research team from the Universitat Politècnica de València and Grupotec published a study revealing a significant gap between expected and actual performance in utility-scale bifacial solar plants. Analyzing data from five sites in Spain and the UK, the researchers found that effective bifaciality often drops by 13% to 15% compared to nominal values. High irradiance and module temperatures were identified as key factors reducing power gains. The study cautions that regulatory factors may overestimate actual energy yields and recommends incorporating variable operating conditions into performance models.
items.title: Study Finds Large Gap Between Expected and Actual Bifacial PV Performance

items.summary: American singer Mary Millben urged young Indians to peacefully protest against the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), alleging it receives funding from US donors opposed to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Millben, who has performed for five US administrations and praised Modi, criticized CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke and accused him of radicalizing US-educated individuals. Her comments follow protests in New Delhi over electoral roll irregularities.
items.title: US Singer Mary Millben Urges Indians to Oppose CJP

items.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni criticized a recent agreement between the United States and Russia to supply over 3,00,000 metric tonnes of diesel. She described the move as a risky choice that undermines efforts to force Vladimir Putin to negotiate with Ukraine. Meloni argued the deal generates revenue for the war and weakens sanctions, while President Donald Trump noted it could lower energy prices in the United States.
items.title: Italy PM Meloni Warns Against US-Russia Diesel Deal

items.summary: UK Health Secretary Yvette Cooper issued a profound apology to parents whose stillborn babies were buried in mass graves without their knowledge between the 1930s and early 1980s. The practice occurred in NHS hospitals, with over 1,000 babies interred in Wirral and another 270 in Royton. Liverpool city council urged the government to provide a written apology and establish a national support framework.
items.title: UK Health Secretary Apologises for Stillborn Baby Burials

items.summary: Researchers from ThreatFabric identified Hirudo, an Android malware that replaces legitimate banking apps to bypass security checks. It targets users in Indonesia, China, India, and other regions by disguising itself within shopping and entertainment apps. The malware steals credentials, controls devices remotely, and captures screenshots. While it retains most original code, leaked keys allow some detection. Experts recommend server-side validation and keeping devices updated.
items.title: Hirudo Malware Evades Android Security to Steal Banking Credentials

items.summary: India's Cabinet approved a ₹52,878 crore sale of a 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank to Fairfax Financial Holdings, marking the largest foreign direct investment in the nation's financial sector. The deal, finalized after five years, transfers control from the government and LIC to Fairfax, subject to regulatory approvals and an open offer to minority shareholders.
items.title: Cabinet Approves Largest FDI Bid for IDBI Bank by Fairfax

items.summary: Digital Editor Jinoy Jose P. recounts how his son, Sangeeth, challenged his rigid scientific explanations of evolution with a simpler, faith-based perspective. During a scooter ride, the boy noted that 'God sounds simpler,' prompting the father to reconsider the value of listening to children's unpolished insights. Jose P. argues that India needs to hear from its youth, who observe the world without adult binaries. He shares a second incident where his son comforted him after a physical punishment, demonstrating the child's emotional maturity. The author concludes that children offer vital lessons on how the nation should behave, urging adults to listen rather than dictate.
items.title: Father Reflects on Listening to Children's Perspectives on Society

items.summary: Andy Burnham responded to questions from Nigel Farage and Kemi Badenoch regarding small boat crossings, Russian interference, and social care reform. He also confirmed that Manchester City did not raise its Premier League charges with him, citing released contact information.
items.title: Andy Burnham Addresses UK Politics and Manchester City Charges in PMQs

items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told NPR that the Trump administration warned it could cut intelligence-sharing unless Ukraine halts long-range drone strikes on Russian oil refineries. Zelenskyy stated he would comply if Russia did the same, but noted Russia targeted a power plant shortly after a similar announcement. Meanwhile, the Vatican announced Pope Leo XIV has been diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma following surgery to remove a growth from his lung. Doctors at Gemelli Hospital in Rome performed the procedure, and experts suggest the cancer was caught early. Trump also ousted ambassador Kimberly Guilfoyle amid allegations of impropriety.
items.title: Zelenskyy Warns of Intelligence Cuts Over Drone Strikes; Pope Diagnosed with Cancer

items.summary: In reports published on October 13, Shekhar Suman stated that Raju Srivastava deserved to win The Great Indian Laughter Challenge, offering a retrospective judgement on the performances. Suman recalled that Raju was hesitant to enter due to fears about his reputation. Although Raju finished third in the 2005 season, Suman encouraged him to view the show as an opportunity rather than focusing solely on winning. This account highlights Suman's perspective on the performer's career dilemma rather than altering the official result.
items.title: Shekhar Suman Says Raju Srivastava Deserved To Win The Great Indian Laughter Challenge

items.summary: Serhiy Beskrestnov, adviser to President Volodymyr Zelensky, warned that overnight speed limits on Starlink terminals are disrupting Ukrainian battlefield missions. A Ukrainian defence ministry source confirmed connectivity restrictions above 160 km/h, which degrade drone operations and logistics. SpaceX has not commented on the reported limits. Zelensky noted at least 600,000 people lost power due to Russian strikes.
items.title: Ukraine Reports Starlink Speed Restrictions Disrupting Military Missions

items.summary: Oman overtook the United States as India's largest liquefied natural gas supplier in September, following a surge in European demand for American cargoes. While U.S. shipments to India dropped significantly, imports from Oman rose, and Nigeria ranked second. India maintained robust demand despite rising tender prices, implementing a strategy to prioritize city gas distribution over industrial sectors.
items.title: Oman Surpasses U.S. as India's Top LNG Supplier in September Amid Global Market Shifts

items.summary: Karanveer Singh, an advocate at the Punjab and Haryana High Court, argues that the right to peaceful protest is a constitutional guarantee under Article 19(1)(b) that does not require state permission. He cites Supreme Court rulings, including Ramlila Maidan Incident (2012) and Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan v. Union of India (2018), which affirm citizens' fundamental right to assemble. Singh distinguishes between 'permission,' which implies state approval, and 'intimation,' a courtesy to ensure public safety. While acknowledging reasonable restrictions under Article 19(3) for public order, he contends that blanket bans or requiring approval from the very entity being protested against violate constitutional principles. The article concludes that the state must recognize this right without granting permission.
items.title: Advocate Argues State Cannot Grant Permission for Peaceful Protest

items.summary: Deputy Neil Inder proposed that reducing civil service posts could finance a 5p cut to white diesel prices. He plans to submit amendments regarding fuel costs amid global events. Inder noted that fuel duty is set to rise by 4.3% in 2027. He stated that the biggest cost to the States is the number of people employed, suggesting stopping recruitment for retiring staff. The BBC has requested comment from the States.
items.title: Guernsey Deputy Suggests Job Cuts Could Fund Diesel Price Drop

items.summary: The FBI arrested Abdulrahman Alfozan, a former OpenAI engineer, for allegedly planting a recording device in a San Francisco office. OpenAI discovered the hidden device and identified Alfozan as the suspect, leading to his arrest on October 9. Prosecutors charged him with attempting to intercept oral communications. If convicted, he faces up to five years in prison and a fine. OpenAI stated it found no evidence of data theft.
items.title: FBI Arrests Saudi OpenAI Employee for Alleged Spy Device

items.summary: Zenzap, a startup building an AI-powered private messenger for workplaces, has raised $44 million in funding. Founded by Guy Weiss in 2022, the company aims to replace consumer apps like WhatsApp and Slack by offering IT-compliant communication tools. The round includes investors Bessemer, Lightspeed, and The Garage. Zenzap currently serves clients such as FedEx and Taco Bell, with 50 staff members globally.
items.title: Zenzap Raises $44M to Build AI Workplace Messenger

items.summary: Sunil Mittal, chairman of Bharti Airtel, stated that Eutelsat OneWeb applied for a satellite communication licence in India five years ago, significantly ahead of Elon Musk's Starlink. Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum 2026, Mittal noted that while OneWeb's ground network has been ready for three years and satellites have hovered over India for five, the company has yet to receive permission to begin services.
items.title: Sunil Mittal Claims OneWeb Satcom Licence Application Precedes Starlink by Five Years

items.summary: Tesla Powerwalls and Sunrun announced a new record for California grid dispatch, reaching 745 MW on October 6. This figure represents a 28% increase from the previous record of 580 MW set in September. Tesla Energy reported that over 85,000 Powerwall owners contributed more than 600 MW, accounting for roughly 80% of the total dispatch. Sunrun, the largest Powerwall channel, stated it was leading the event. The dispatch occurred during an October heat wave at the request of the California Energy Commission and state utilities to meet peak demand. Sunrun CEO Mary Powell noted that customers are being compensated for helping strengthen grid reliability. The companies plan to expand this capability with a Google-funded distributed power plant in the San Jose area, aiming to enroll nearly 21,000 devices as part of a 16.8 GW virtual power plant plan.
items.title: Tesla Powerwalls and Sunrun Set New California Grid Dispatch Record

items.summary: Microsoft resolved a bug in Always On VPN triggered by September 2026 Windows 11 security updates. The issue caused connections to fail or remain stuck if automatic protocol selection was configured. Microsoft released cumulative updates KB5127648 and KB5127646 to fix the problem. Administrators can temporarily mitigate the issue by selecting a single protocol, either SSTP or IKEv2, instead of automatic selection.
items.title: Microsoft Resolves VPN Connection Issues from September Updates

items.summary: The European Commission stated it is in dialogue with Google regarding potential responses to $1 billion fines and required changes to its app store and search engine. Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier confirmed the ongoing discussions without prejudging the outcome. The Commission ordered Google to treat rivals fairly and allow developers to steer users away from Google Play within 60 days. Google has begun implementing some changes to search results and service fees.
items.title: EU Commission in Dialogue with Google Over Antitrust Fines

items.summary: Microsoft and OpenAI executives called for new artificial intelligence safety laws at the International AI Summit 2026 in Ireland. Brad Smith stated that companies must prevent harm rather than just warn of risks, noting AI capabilities have advanced faster than protections. OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar supported global regulation, emphasizing the need to ensure cyber defenders have the tools to counter malicious actors while maintaining transparency.
items.title: Microsoft and OpenAI Executives Urge AI Safety Laws

items.summary: Bharti Airtel stated its satellite venture with Eutelsat OneWeb is significantly ahead of Elon Musk's Starlink in India's licensing queue, having applied five years ago. Founder Sunil Mittal noted their ground networks are ready but services await permission. This follows Musk's allegations of business interests blocking Starlink, which the Ministry of Communications rejected as baseless. Reliance's Jio Satcom and Amazon's Leo also hold licenses or seek them.
items.title: Bharti Airtel Claims Satcom Approval Ahead of Starlink

items.summary: Meta has launched a new AI feature called 'Your Algorithm' for Facebook users. This tool allows users to customize their feed and reels by selecting topics and providing feedback in their own language, giving them more control over content recommendations.
items.title: Meta Launches New AI Feature to Let Users Control Facebook Algorithm

items.summary: Anthropic warns that advances in small AI models may enable self-replicating malware capable of infecting IoT devices like smart fridges and vacuum cleaners. While an internal experiment revealed challenges in creating such a replicator, the company notes it could be difficult to stop due to the lack of a centralized shutdown point. The models could autonomously configure themselves on unfamiliar hardware, potentially propagating without human interaction.
items.title: Anthropic Warns Small AI Models Could Self-Replicate on IoT Devices

items.summary: Apple growers in south Kashmir face financial pressure as daily labour rates for apple picking have surged to between ₹1,000 and ₹1,500, more than double the usual ₹600 to ₹650. While official data reports an average wage of ₹660.77 in January 2026, growers report struggling to find affordable workers during the peak harvest season, threatening their ability to recover input costs and maintain fruit quality.
items.title: Rising Labour Wages Strain Kashmir Apple Growers

items.summary: The Indian government approved the sale of a 60.72 per cent controlling stake in IDBI Bank to Fairfax Financial Holdings for Rs 52,878 crore. This transaction concludes a nine-year journey involving regulatory restrictions, a takeover by LIC, and multiple bidding rounds. Following the deal, the government and LIC will retain a 34 per cent stake.
items.title: Government Approves IDBI Bank Stake Sale to Fairfax

items.summary: Apple and OpenAI are set for a critical court hearing regarding allegations of trade secret theft. Apple requests an order halting OpenAI's use of allegedly stolen information, while OpenAI seeks to dismiss the lawsuit entirely. The dispute involves Apple accusing OpenAI of extracting confidential data through job interviews and employee defections. OpenAI denies these claims, arguing the suit targets ordinary job interviews and highlights weaknesses in Apple's security practices. The case centers on whether OpenAI improperly accessed Apple's proprietary product designs and supply chain details. A preliminary injunction could require OpenAI to stop using acquired confidential information immediately.
items.title: Apple and OpenAI Clash in High-Stakes Trade Secret Lawsuit Hearing

items.summary: OpenAI stated it identified, fired, and reported to the FBI an employee who bugged its office. Abdulrahman Alfozan, a Saudi national, was arrested and charged with illegally recording company communication. Evidence included chatbot logs regarding device installation. Jay Clayton cited the case as proof the White House AI task force is needed.
items.title: Saudi national arrested for allegedly planting recording device at OpenAI

items.summary: New York University professor John Perrino reports that while over 60 countries explore social media age restrictions, only seven have implemented bans. Perrino notes a global trend favoring safety-by-design requirements over full prohibitions due to technical, legal, and social challenges. Examples include Australia's low compliance rates and legal challenges in the UK and France. Perrino highlights that governments increasingly prioritize accountability and safer service design, citing the EU KIDS Act and Mexico's rejection of an outright ban following expert consultations.
items.title: Global Shift from Social Media Bans to Safety-By-Design Regulations

items.summary: US mortgage rates reached 7.5%, the highest level since November 2023, according to Mortgage Bankers Association data. Consequently, home purchasing activity declined for a sixth consecutive week, marking the longest such stretch since July-August 2023. Lawrence Yun of the National Association of Realtors noted that fourth-quarter closing activity will likely decrease due to these higher rates.
items.title: Rising US Mortgage Rates Drive Sixth Week of Home-Buying Slump

items.summary: ASML reported record quarterly sales of €11.7 billion but warned its machine supply will not fully meet AI-driven demand in 2027 and 2028. CEO Christophe Fouquet stated the company is investigating ways to increase capacity beyond previously communicated levels. Analysts note durable growth continues, though questions remain about potential downturns starting in 2029.
items.title: ASML Reports Record Sales but Warns of Future Supply Shortages

items.summary: US consumer prices accelerated in September, driven largely by a surge in fuel costs, complicating the Federal Reserve's upcoming October interest rate decision. The Consumer Price Index rose 0.6%, with petrol prices jumping 9.1%. Core inflation, excluding food and energy, gained 0.3%. Markets now see a roughly 52% chance of a rate hike at the Fed's Oct 27-28 meeting, up from 22% previously. The data adds pressure to President Donald Trump and his party ahead of the Nov 3 midterm elections, as rising costs continue to erode consumer sentiment and approval ratings. Jeffrey Roach of LPL Financial noted the road to price stability remains difficult.
items.title: Rising US Inflation Revives October Fed Rate Hike Prospects Amid Political Pressure

items.summary: American Electric Power plans to invest approximately $4 billion in a 702-megawatt fuel cell facility near Cheyenne, Wyoming, to power Google. The project, using Bloom Energy technology and carbon capture, is expected to be operational by the end of 2028 under a 20-year agreement. AEP Chairman Bill Fehrman stated the initiative aims to deliver reliable, innovative energy solutions at scale.
items.title: AEP Plans $4 Billion Wyoming Fuel Cell Plant for Google

items.summary: Sugarcane growers in Haveri and Dharwad districts withdrew highway blockades on Wednesday evening following marathon talks with officials. Although the protests disrupted transport for two days, authorities persuaded the farmers to clear the road. The growers, led by Bhuvaneshwar Shidlapur, now plan a foot march to Hubballi. While full highway access remains restricted, movement of vehicles has resumed on partial lanes.
items.title: Sugarcane Growers Withdraw Highway Blockades After Marathon Talks

items.summary: Leader of Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan cautioned the Kerala government against pursuing nuclear power projects, citing potential future risks. He noted that recent Central amendments removed stringent liability conditions for operators. While the state government previously urged increased power generation via solar, hydro, and nuclear options in a fiscal white paper, Vijayan advised caution regarding immediate nuclear adoption.
items.title: Opposition Leader Warns Kerala Against Nuclear Power Push Amid Power Crisis

items.summary: Congress leaders Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra met Ankita Bhandari's parents at India Gate regarding the appointment of Dushyant Kumar Gautam as Sikkim Governor. The family, whose daughter was murdered in 2022, demands the appointment be paused until the CBI probe concludes. They allege Gautam is linked to the case and threatened a hunger strike if their request is ignored. The appointment remains unproven, and Gautam has initiated defamation proceedings.
items.title: Congress Leaders Meet Parents of Ankita Bhandari Over Governor Appointment

items.summary: Economists surveyed by FactSet forecast US consumer prices rose 3.6% in September, up from 3.4% in August. Analysts attribute the increase to higher gas prices and supply shocks from the Iran war, alongside rising semiconductor costs. The data underscores persistent inflation challenges for the Federal Reserve and political issues for Republicans in Congress.
items.title: Economists forecast US inflation rise driven by gas and chip costs

items.summary: Union minister Chirag Paswan challenged Rahul Gandhi to resign, citing his and his sister's electoral victories as proof of the process's integrity. While condemning police brutality against students protesting Special Intensive Revision irregularities, Paswan alleged anti-social elements infiltrated the demonstrations. Conversely, Rahul Gandhi met injured students, urged PM Narendra Modi not to obstruct them, and promised justice for alleged police actions.
items.title: Chirag Paswan Challenges Rahul Gandhi to Resign Amid SIR Protests

items.summary: A Lynx M20S robot developed by DEEP Robotics aided researchers in the Ailao Mountains of Yunnan Province, China, to document rare ghost plants and the western black-crested gibbon. The robot's low-angle imaging and ability to advance observation positions by about 20 meters allowed access to dense forests and steep terrains difficult for conventional field observations. This survey, conducted with the China Association for Scientific Expedition, highlights how technology supports biodiversity surveys in hard-to-reach environments.
items.title: Robot Assists Researchers in Documenting Rare Plants and Gibbons in China

items.summary: China's Pinglu Canal project received the Green Design International Award and Green Design International Contribution Award at the World Canals Conference 2026 in Guilin. The World Green Design Organization presented the honors on October 13, 2026. The 134.2-kilometer waterway, which opened on September 16, connects the Xijiang River network with the Beibu Gulf.
items.title: Pinglu Canal Project Wins International Green Design Awards

items.summary: China's service exports grew 14.8% year on year in the first eight months of 2026, reaching 2 trillion yuan, according to the Ministry of Commerce. Knowledge-intensive services led the increase, contributing 53.7% of export growth, while personal, cultural, and recreational services rose 66%. The total services trade reached 5.07 trillion yuan, up 7.9%, narrowing the trade deficit by 145.12 billion yuan.
items.title: China's Service Exports Rise Driven by Knowledge-Intensive Sectors

items.summary: Lunar samples from the near and far sides of the moon will be displayed at the 16th China International Aviation and Aerospace Exhibition, according to the State Administration of Science, Technology and Industry for National Defense. Yi Lin, a Chinese defense industry official, noted that visitors can observe the differences between samples brought back by Chang'e-5 and Chang'e-6. The exhibition, held in Zhuhai from December 7 to 13, features expanded indoor areas and showcases various aerospace achievements.
items.title: Lunar Samples from Near and Far Sides to Display at Airshow China

items.summary: The Singapore Land Authority (SLA) announced an extension of lease tenancies for four master tenants at Punggol East and Tebing Lane until December 31, 2027. This decision follows a review of operational challenges faced by affected businesses. The extension aims to provide additional time for these entities to manage their transition and relocation, acknowledging the difficulties involved in securing alternative premises before the original expiry date of December 31, 2026.
items.title: Singapore Land Authority Grants Lease Extension to Punggol Businesses

items.summary: At the DBS Asia Future Forward Conference, DBS CEO Tan Su Shan and TikTok CEO Chew Shou Zi stressed the necessity of human judgment in AI applications. The article argues that for employees to genuinely oversee AI decisions, organizations must create conditions allowing them time, training, and the freedom to challenge recommendations without fear of penalty. Accountability must extend to the organizations setting performance targets.
items.title: DBS CEO and TikTok Chief Emphasize Human Judgment in AI Use

items.summary: Advocate Abhisht Hela gained attention for representing leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) following their detention by Delhi Police over access to Jantar Mantar. The site's designated protest status was withdrawn a day before the activists were detained for allegedly entering without authorization. Hela, founder of Hela & Associates Law Chambers, challenged the Special Executive Magistrate's authority to remand leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka to five days of judicial custody. He also contested Delhi Police allegations regarding bond violations. While Das and Ranka were detained, leader Ajinkya Shinde was released on a personal bond. The incident occurs amidst ongoing agitation by the CJP against the Chief Election Commissioner.
items.title: Advocate Abhisht Hela Represents Detained CJP Leaders in Jantar Mantar Dispute

items.summary: The Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation organized a week-long Right to Information Act awareness program across Coimbatore, Erode, Tiruppur, and the Nilgiris districts. Led by Managing Director S. Gopalakrishnan, the initiative aimed to curb corruption and enhance responsibility. In 2025, the corporation addressed 2,658 petitions, with half concerning employee terminal benefits. Official sources noted 800 petitions were handled in Coimbatore alone this year.
items.title: TNSTC Launches RTI Awareness Drive to Promote Transparency

items.summary: Jason O’Connell, a Reform UK Senedd member, faced scrutiny after using smart glasses during a speech in the Senedd chamber. This incident prompted calls for a ban on such devices in Westminster. The Liberal Democrats urged the speaker to act, citing risks to privacy and security. A review is underway to address the implications of these emerging technologies in parliamentary settings.
items.title: Calls for Ban on Smart Glasses in Westminster Following Reform Politician's Use

items.summary: Following the five-day judicial custody of Janata Party leaders in Tihar Jail, Abhijeet Dipke called for a demonstration on October 16 at 5:00 PM in Connaught Place. TMC MP Mahua Moitra expressed full backing for the protest against alleged electoral malpractice. She stated that the resignation of Union Home Minister Amit Shah should be on the table, while also implicating senior government leadership in the movement's broader accountability goals.
items.title: TMC MP Mahua Moitra Supports Protest Call Amid Judicial Custody Tensions

items.summary: Police arrested Ebin B Paul, 32, for setting fire to Blossom Nursery near a synagogue in Kochi on October 12 at 2.30 am. The accused allegedly recorded the act and fled. Investigators found suspicious online communications and alleged links to foreign-based individuals, probing a potential terror angle and wider conspiracy. While police suspect international connections and an unidentified handler, these links remain under investigation. National agencies, including the NIA, are involved due to the site's international significance. Authorities are also examining possible cryptocurrency payments and a connection to a prior arson in Muvattupuzha.
items.title: Man Arrested for Arson Near Kochi Synagogue Amid Terror Probe

items.summary: The European Commission stated there is no indication that US intelligence sharing with Ukraine has stopped, despite reports of Starlink disruptions. Meanwhile, Zelenskyy met with UK and EU leaders to discuss support and regional security concerns.
items.title: EU confirms US intelligence sharing with Ukraine continues amid attacks

items.summary: A fire at a Bochum, Germany residential building killed three Indians and injured five. Police arrested a 41-year-old Romanian resident on murder suspicion. Investigators suspect arson but are still examining whether the blaze was deliberate or accidental. Victims' identities remain undisclosed. Firefighters faced difficulties as flames spread through stairwells.
items.title: Three Indians Killed in Bochum Fire; Suspect Arrested

items.summary: France's cybersecurity authority warned that a cyberattack targeting supermarket refrigeration systems may still be underway, causing temperatures to surge and forcing the disposal of goods. Approximately 700 of the country's 10,000 supermarkets were affected, with the Intermarché chain reporting losses of tens of millions of euros in a single day. Authorities advise retailers to use secure connections and update firmware. While the precise attack method remains undisclosed, experts suggest older systems and inadequate security practices were exploited. No perpetrators have been identified, and investigations are ongoing. A separate, unlinked incident recently affected Dutch supermarkets.
items.title: France Warns Refrigeration Cyberattacks May Persist Amid Supermarket Disruptions

items.summary: Floqer, an autonomous customer knowledge platform, is pitching at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 and plans to open-source its database technology in early 2027 pending security reviews. Founded in 2024, the company reports $1.2 million in annual recurring revenue and claims customers reduce prospecting time by up to 70%. CEO Shivam Mahajan cites customer demand and a desire for data sovereignty as drivers for the move.
items.title: Floqer to Open-Source AI Database Amid High Demand

items.summary: Unseasonable heat in the Midwest and Mid-Atlantic coincided with PJM's fall maintenance season, causing power prices to top $1,000. With roughly 62,000 megawatts offline for planned work, PJM issued a Maximum Generation Alert. The grid serving 67 million people is running thin as demand approaches all-time peaks, prompting emergency measures and regulatory scrutiny over capacity planning.
items.title: PJM Grid Faces Strain from Heat and Maintenance

items.summary: Turkish police raided Halk TV in Istanbul, citing financial crimes against chairman Cafer Mahiroglu, who lives abroad and rejected the allegations as politically motivated. Eleven of 17 sought individuals were detained. The raid sparked outrage, with opposition politicians and press freedom organizations condemning the intervention. Amnesty International called for the broadcaster's independence to be restored, highlighting concerns over media freedom in Turkey.
items.title: Turkish Police Raid Halk TV Over Alleged Financial Crimes

items.summary: The All India Loco Running Staff Association (AILRSA), South Zone, urged the Eighth Central Pay Commission to assess Loco Running staff pay and conditions via scientific job analysis. The association highlighted irregular biological work patterns and high responsibility. Although a Madras High Court order from April 26, 2022, directed this analysis, subsequent legal proceedings delayed the process. AILRSA secretary V. Balachandran called for immediate completion.
items.title: AILRSA South Zone Urges Scientific Job Evaluation for Loco Pilots

items.summary: Aaron Day is launching a national campaign to use third-party candidates as spoilers to cost Republicans Senate seats, a strategy he previously used against Kelly Ayotte in 2016. Day plans to spend up to $2.5 million on AI-generated ads to boost Libertarian and other minor party candidates in eight targeted states. While Republican leaders remain skeptical, Day argues his approach holds major parties accountable. The plan relies on the theory that small shifts in vote share in close races can flip outcomes, a tactic supported by past results in Nevada and Montana. However, some third-party candidates, like Ted Brown, state they run to win rather than merely disrupt.
items.title: Aaron Day Plans National Spoiler Campaign to Disrupt Senate Races

items.summary: Congress general secretary Sachin Pilot stated there is no personal animosity between him and senior colleague Ashok Gehlot, asserting they must work unitedly to defeat the BJP in Rajasthan's 2028 assembly polls. Pilot dismissed claims of a promised chief ministerial post, noting politics involves no guarantees. He emphasized that while Gehlot, as an elder, has more latitude to speak, both leaders have worked closely. Pilot highlighted the need for the entire party leadership to fight the 'double engine' of the central and state governments. The two leaders previously shared strained ties, but recent friendly banter suggests a resolution. Pilot also pledged to campaign for Gehlot's son in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls.
items.title: Pilot denies personal animosity with Gehlot as Congress leaders unite for 2028 polls

items.summary: Three Indian nationals died in a fire at a residential building in Bochum, Germany, on October 13, 2026. Five others were injured. Investigators suspect arson but are still investigating the cause. Police arrested a 41-year-old Romanian resident on suspicion of murder. Details of the victims' identities remain undisclosed.
items.title: Three Indians Killed in Bochum Fire; Suspect Arrested

items.summary: Singapore is keeping options open for prosecution under the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act while reviewing data on the ongoing haze situation, said Minister Grace Fu. Hourly PM2.5 readings hit 288 in the west, the highest since 2015, prompting facility closures and mask distribution. Fu expressed hope Indonesia controls fires despite difficult El Nino conditions and offered general assistance.
items.title: Singapore Keeps Prosecution Options Open Amid Haze Crisis

items.summary: An inquest heard that 17-year-old Connor Bell died after being accidentally shot in the head with an air rifle by his friend Jack Beechy at a house party in Basingstoke. Beechy mistook the trigger for the safety catch while the weapon was pointed at Bell. The coroner ruled the death an accident caused by a gunshot wound to the head.
items.title: Inquest hears accidental air rifle shooting killed 17-year-old boy at Hampshire party

items.summary: Italian industry minister Adolfo Urso stated that Chinese automakers have ruled out Italy for new production facilities due to a lack of suitable turnkey factories. Urso noted that Stellantis, Italy's major producer, has not closed any plants and thus has no facilities to hand over. BYD's European adviser Alfredo Altavilla confirmed that BYD aims to fully own a European plant, focusing on Spain and France instead.
items.title: Italian Minister Says Chinese Automakers Ruled Out Italy For Factories

items.summary: External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar is set to visit the United Arab Emirates from October 14-16, 2026, for bilateral meetings and the Raisina Middle East event. The visit highlights India-UAE strategic ties as global oil markets face volatility due to US-Iran tensions and supply fluctuations projected by the IEA.
items.title: EAM Jaishankar to visit UAE for strategic partnership review amid global oil volatility

items.summary: Ameresco completed a $1 million solar-plus-storage project at the Roseburg Urban Sanitary Authority in Oregon. The 39.4-kW solar system generates approximately 51,580 kWh annually, offsetting 100% of the main office's electricity. An 184-kWh battery ensures power availability during disruptions. Future phases will add solar systems at the wastewater and natural treatment facilities, with construction anticipated before year-end.
items.title: Ameresco Completes Solar and Storage Project for Oregon Wastewater Authority

items.summary: Marine Le Pen maintains a 35% to 37% lead in the 2027 French presidential election first round, according to a poll by RTL and Toluna Harris Interactive. Her support remains stable despite allegations against party leader Jordan Bardella regarding 2013 antisemitic writings. The survey indicates Le Pen scores higher on leadership and ambition metrics compared to Bardella.
items.title: Le Pen Leads 2027 Poll Despite Bardella Controversy

items.summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) announced on Wednesday the seizure of assets worth Rs 2,032.81 crore from Anil Ambani-led Reliance Power Limited. These assets, including bank balances and shareholding in Sasan Power Limited, were taken under the Foreign Exchange Management Act. The agency stated the value matches foreign exchange held outside India in contravention of FEMA Section 4.
items.title: ED Seizes Rs 2,032.81 Crore Assets from Reliance Power

items.summary: Three motorcyclists skidded on Kolkata's Chingrighata flyover, painted in rainbow colors for Durga Puja, raising safety concerns. Police confirmed no injuries, though the cause remains unascertained. Experts warn that decorative paint reduces friction on wet roads, validating earlier warnings. Officials have deployed a team to inspect the surfaces and report findings, while the government notes the paint is temporary.
items.title: Rainbow Paint on Kolkata Flyovers Sparks Safety Concerns After Accidents

items.summary: Fishers in northeastern Brazil have removed at least 440 invasive lionfish from the Abrolhos reefs. The local government paid 10 Brazilian reais per fish to curb the species' spread, which threatens native stocks. Researchers analyzed 430 specimens to assess the impact. While the invasion was confirmed in June 2026, its full extent remains unmeasured as officials gather data to determine feasible measures.
items.title: Fishers Remove Invasive Lionfish from Brazil's Abrolhos Reefs

items.summary: The jaguarundi was recently recategorized from least concern to near threatened on the IUCN Red List, reports contributor Sean Mowbray for Mongabay. Researchers attribute the decline to human-wildlife conflict, dangerous roadways, attacks by dogs, and infectious disease. Although the species is frequently seen in open areas, Tadeu de Oliveira notes that quantifying the data reveals a different reality, prompting hopes for increased conservation attention.
items.title: Jaguarundi Recategorized to Near Threatened Despite Common Sightings

items.summary: Seventeen-year-old Yash Sambhaji Mulik broke the Indian Under-18 national record in the 110-metre hurdles with a time of 13. 40 seconds, surpassing the previous mark of 13. 47 seconds held by Kiran K. Selected by the School Games Federation of India, Mulik will represent the nation at the ISF Gymnasiade 2026 in Rio de Janeiro from December 3 to 8. The athlete, a Class 12 student, balances his studies with evening training sessions at Father Agnel gymkhana in Ghansoli, Navi Mumbai.
items.title: Yash Mulik Shatters U-18 Hurdles Record to Represent India

items.summary: Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra met Ankita Bhandari's family at India Gate to protest the appointment of BJP leader Dushyant Gautam as Sikkim's Governor. The family opposes the move due to unresolved questions and alleged VIP involvement in Bhandari's 2022 murder. Uttarakhand Congress president Ganesh Godiyal also staged a hunger strike demanding transparency in the investigation.
items.title: Congress Leaders Meet Ankita Bhandari Family at India Gate

items.summary: The Supreme Court rejected the Election Commission's claim that it lost video recordings of the 2023 Karnataka Assembly vote count. During a dispute between Congress leader TD Rajegowda and BJP's DN Jeevaraj, the bench warned the commission to produce the missing footage or face adverse inferences. The court directed the EC to submit the election observer's report and original counting videos by the next date.
items.title: Supreme Court Rejects EC's Loss of Karnataka Vote Videos

items.summary: Wood Mackenzie reports India's natural gas demand fell by 1.5 million tons this year as the Iran war disrupted Middle East LNG supplies. While Bangladesh and Pakistan faced sharper declines, India's diversified supplier base, including the US and Nigeria, helped mitigate the impact. Tender prices rose to $26.4/MMBtu by September, yet demand remained robust.
items.title: Iran War Reduces India's Gas Demand Amid Rising LNG Prices

items.summary: US inflation rose to 3.7% in September, the highest annual rate since spring, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. This figure marks the highest pre-midterm inflation since 1990, excluding the pandemic. Polls indicate widespread dissatisfaction with the Trump administration over rising costs, with 78% of Americans blaming current policies. The White House did not immediately respond to inquiries about the report.
items.title: US Inflation Hits 3.7% in September, Striking Republicans Before Midterms

items.summary: Delhi University's Executive Council approved ₹5,889 crore in hostel projects to address a persistent shortage of affordable student accommodation. The plan includes new facilities and the reconstruction of existing hostels, aiming to increase capacity for 21,895 students. While the university's highest decision-making body cleared the proposals, they require further approval from the Union Ministry of Education before implementation. Vice-Chancellor Yogesh Singh noted that the planning considers future needs for the next 100 years. However, delays in previous projects and pending funding from the Union Ministry of Women and Child Development remain concerns. The university currently houses around 7,224 students, with over 251,000 enrolled across its programs.
items.title: Delhi University Approves Major Hostel Expansion Plan Amid Housing Shortage

items.summary: The Supreme Court criticized the Election Commission of India for failing to produce a video recording of the 2023 vote count in Karnataka's Sringeri constituency. During a dispute between Congress's TD Rajegowda and BJP's DN Jeevaraj, the bench warned that it would draw an adverse inference if the ECI could not provide the records by the next hearing. The court rejected the commission's claim that the footage was lost.
items.title: Supreme Court warns ECI over missing 2023 vote-counting video

items.summary: Standard Solar has acquired two solar projects in Washington from OneEnergy Renewables, marking their first collaboration in the state. The Palouse Junction and Cunningham projects will add 15.79 MW of ground-mounted capacity to eastern Washington. Franklin Public Utility District and Big Bend Electric Cooperative will serve as offtakers. Both projects are expected to be completed in Q1 2027.
items.title: Standard Solar Acquires Two Washington Solar Projects from OneEnergy Renewables

items.summary: More than 300,000 public sector workers, including nurses and teachers, are striking across the Republic of Ireland amid a pay dispute with the government. A further strike is planned for 21 October. Union leaders cite government inaction as the cause, while ministers warn of significant economic disruption and cancelled hospital appointments. Teachers describe the financial situation as unfeasible.
items.title: Hundreds of Thousands of Workers Strike Across Republic of Ireland

items.summary: Ofwat announced that several English and Welsh water providers must return money to customers because they missed performance targets. Yorkshire Water and Thames Water face penalties of £75.1m and £45.8m respectively, while other firms like Dŵr Cymru and United Utilities also face reductions. Conversely, Severn Trent and Northumbrian Water will receive reward payments for meeting targets. The regulator stated that overall, the industry is expected to cut bills by a net £240m for failures during 2025-26, with £107m returned via lower bills in 2027-28. Ofwat noted these figures are still at the draft stage and final decisions will be made by 15 December, taking effect from 1 April 2027.
items.title: Ofwat Orders Water Firms to Return Millions via Lower Bills

items.summary: Ford is inviting buyers to sign up for preorder invites for the upcoming Fathom electric pickup, with official preorders set to open in early 2027. The vehicle is priced to start under $30,000, utilizing a lithium iron phosphate battery platform. While specific range and towing figures remain unannounced, the company highlights features like Apple Maps integration and BlueCruise hands-free driving capabilities.
items.title: Ford invites preorders for the $30,000 Fathom EV pickup

items.summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued five post-inspection observations to Zydus Lifesciences' manufacturing plant in Moraiya, Ahmedabad. The inspection took place from October 5-13. Zydus Lifesciences stated on Tuesday that it will work closely with the FDA to address the observations expeditiously. The report was published on October 14, 2026.
items.title: Zydus Lifesciences Receives Five FDA Observations Following Plant Inspection

items.summary: A Meerut court sentenced Muskan Rastogi and Sahil Shukla to death for murdering Saurabh Rajput, dismembering his body, and concealing it in a cement-filled blue drum. The merchant navy officer died on March 3, 2025. After 126 hearings over 13 months, District Judge Arvind Kumar Mishra pronounced the verdict on October 14, noting the case captured national headlines for its grisly details.
items.title: Muskan and Sahil Sentenced to Death for 'Blue Drum' Murder

items.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has worsened, with confirmed cases surpassing 9,000 and deaths exceeding 4,300. Health authorities struggle to contain the epidemic across seven provinces. Dr Catherine Swallwood of the World Health Organization notes that many deaths occur outside treatment centres, with about 60 per cent of cases being community deaths. Consequently, the WHO is shifting focus to remote and hard-to-access areas.
items.title: WHO alarmed by surge in Ebola deaths outside treatment centres in DR Congo

items.summary: Security researcher Sila Ozeren Hacioglu of Picus Security explains that while agentic pentesting allows rapid exploitation testing, it suffers from blind spots regarding reachability and lack of public exploits. Omdia research indicates organizations typically test only 32% of their attack surface. Picus demonstrates how its Exposure Validation method fills these gaps by analyzing attacker behaviors against live controls rather than relying solely on successful exploitation. The approach converts raw findings into evidence-backed priorities, enabling teams to validate every CVE on every asset within hours.
items.title: Picus Security Addresses Blind Spots in Agentic Pentesting

items.summary: Pakistan and Turkey have activated the Mecca mutual defence pact to provide military support to Saudi Arabia following Houthi attacks, though they are not engaging in direct combat. While Pakistan deploys reconnaissance assets and existing troops, Turkey faces parliamentary delays. Analysts view this as a stress test for the alliance, noting its defensive nature contrasts with NATO's integrated command. The pact aims to free Saudi forces for offensive operations while protecting holy sites, but risks mission creep if the conflict expands to Sanaa. Washington sees the arrangement as a convenience for intelligence sharing rather than combat assistance.
items.title: Pakistan and Turkey Deploy Forces to Support Saudi Arabia Against Houthis

items.summary: ZDNET reports that the October Windows update addresses over 1,400 security flaws, marking the final supported update for Windows 11 24H2. The patch includes fixes for 80 critical vulnerabilities and two zero-days, one of which has already been exploited in the wild. The update also resolves issues with File Explorer and Bluetooth while introducing new settings for the Copilot key.
items.title: Microsoft October Update Patches 1,400 Security Flaws

items.summary: Noel Tata and his son Neville filed caveats in the Bombay High Court and Mumbai City Civil Court regarding a dispute involving Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh. Sources reported the move on October 14, 2026, noting the filings were made on October 7. The caveats aim to ensure the matter is heard before orders are passed. The conflict involves allegations of governance lapses at Tata Trusts, which holds a 66% stake in Tata Sons, amidst broader disputes over the group's listing.
items.title: Tata Trusts Chairperson and Son File Caveats in Court Over Governance Dispute

items.summary: The Crown Prosecutor opened the prosecution case in Russell Brand's trial for multiple sex offences at London's Southwark Crown Court. Describing Brand as a 'ruthless, calculated and manipulative sexual predator', the prosecutor stated that women were 'simply a means to an end' to him. The 51-year-old entertainer faces seven charges, including rape and sexual assault, relating to six women over a 10-year period starting in 1999. Brand has pleaded not guilty to all counts. Witness Mark Pinheiro testified that Brand once said he hoped to sleep with 5,000 girls. The trial is expected to last at least six weeks.
items.title: Prosecution Opens Case Against Russell Brand on Sex Offence Charges

items.summary: Waiting times for driving tests dropped below 20 weeks for the first time since November 2024, averaging 19.7 weeks in September. The Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency (DVSA) aims to clear a backlog originating from the 2020 pandemic. Despite progress, officials admit targets for reducing waits to seven weeks by summer 2026 may not be met until next autumn.
items.title: Driving Test Waits Fall to Two-Year Low Amid Ongoing Backlog

items.summary: NVIDIA announced that semiconductor leaders are adopting its CUDA-X libraries to advance AI-defined fabs, where artificial intelligence optimizes chip manufacturing. The new cuPotential library accelerates atomic-scale simulations by 2-3x, while other tools speed up inspection and design workflows. Companies like Lam Research, KLA, and Synopsys report significant performance gains, with some simulations running up to 30x faster. NVIDIA executives stated that AI is transforming how chips are built, enabling engineers to manage complexity and improve yield as demand for advanced chips rises.
items.title: NVIDIA Partners With Semiconductor Leaders to Advance AI-Defined Fabs

items.summary: Siemens and NVIDIA demonstrated how to improve the reliability of AI agents in chip design workflows using the NVIDIA NeMo Gym library. The Siemens Fuse EDA AI Agent, which automates standard-cell characterization, previously generated plausible but incorrect artifacts. By implementing a domain-specific verifier to evaluate final Liberty files against reference data, the team identified failure modes missed by intermediate checks. Refining the agent's skills and tool descriptions increased the composite verification score from approximately 55% to 95%, while reducing agent turns and output tokens. The study highlights the necessity of end-to-end evaluation for trustworthy automation in engineering domains.
items.title: Siemens and NVIDIA Improve Chip Design Agent Reliability

items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated the company would not stop supplying chips to unsafe developers without prior conversation, citing that their technology is general-purpose. Huang announced a $250 million donation for UK AI safety research. He noted fears are part of industry growth and that AI can monitor itself. Nvidia stock fell 2% following a separate proposal to slow AI development.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Discusses AI Safety and Chip Supply

items.summary: Researchers conducted a comprehensive review of 34 scientific papers to map wildlife trafficking patterns in the Brazilian Amazon, identifying 137 species. Birds accounted for 36.4% of trades, followed by mammals, reptiles, and fish. Key drivers include religious rituals, medicine, and food consumption. Neighboring countries like Colombia serve as export hubs, laundering animals before they reach international markets. The study highlights a significant information gap due to scattered data and limited research funding, noting that many seizures are not recorded in official statistics. The findings aim to support investigators and shape protection strategies for the region's biodiversity.
items.title: Researchers Map Hidden Routes of Amazon Wildlife Trafficking

items.summary: Democratic lawmakers in Massachusetts requested a new environmental review from the FAA regarding a planned Amazon Prime Air drone delivery hub west of Boston. Citing concerns over noise, health, safety, and privacy, Senators Ed Markey and Elizabeth Warren, along with Representatives Jim McGovern and Lori Trahan, wrote to FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford. The request follows a lawsuit by 15 states challenging the agency's existing drone rules.
items.title: Lawmakers Urge FAA Review of Amazon Drone Hub Near Boston

items.summary: Jagran (SJM), an RSS affiliate, urged the Union government to deny Starlink a commercial satellite broadband licence in India, citing national security risks. Ashwani Mahajan, SJM's national co-convenor, argued that satellite internet could hinder authorities' ability to restrict services during law-and-order situations and allow hostile actors to communicate. The group emphasized the need for domestic gateways and referenced security concerns in other nations.
items.title: RSS Affiliate Urges India to Deny Starlink Licence Over Security Fears

items.summary: The FBI arrested Abdulrahman Alfozan, an OpenAI engineer, for allegedly planting a recording device in a restricted conference room. Authorities allege he wrapped the USB device in toilet paper and plugged it into a television to spy on confidential discussions. OpenAI discovered the device two days after it was likely planted and subsequently cut off Alfozan's access while cooperating with the FBI.
items.title: FBI Arrests OpenAI Engineer for Planted Recording Device

items.summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra assert that recent forex curbs will stabilize the rupee, which has depreciated 2.8% since April 1, 2026. While acknowledging strong reserves, they warn that rising wholesale inflation of 11.39% in September signals production cost pressures. They argue that while interest rates offer short-term relief, credible fiscal management and supply-side reforms are essential for long-term stability and attracting foreign investment.
items.title: India's Finance Minister and RBI Governor Address Forex Volatility and Fiscal Risks

items.summary: Demis Hassabis, co-founder of Google DeepMind, described recent AI-driven hacking incidents as early warning shots for future major security breaches. Speaking at a summit in Dublin, he urged the industry to adopt rigorous security standards and international regulations to prevent escalation. Microsoft's Brad Smith echoed these concerns, calling for urgent safety laws to match rapid technological innovation.
items.title: Google DeepMind's Hassabis warns of AI hacking risks

items.summary: Sriram Raghavan, General Manager of IBM Software in India, argues that use-case-based regulation is the most effective approach for governing AI. Speaking to businessline, he suggests treating AI like any other technology rather than creating an overarching law.
